deckTitle: The Great Kayfabe Improv Komedy SKETCHBOOK

cards.cardName: The Great Kayfabe Improv Komedy SKETCHBOOK
cards.power: Print. Cut. Sabotage reality.
cards.lore: You are playing a game about playing a game. Try to keep up.
cards.gradeReason: Three-word performance manifesto. Shortest complete instruction in the deck.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: ink+watercolor. Subject: yellow rabbit painting CORPORATE REALITY with giant brush. Mood: meta-sabotage.

cards.power: Destroy this book. Cut the cards. Shuffle them. See what happens.
cards.lore: No board. No pawns. No manual thicker than your wrist. That was a design decision, not laziness. Probably.
cards.gradeReason: "See what happens" — the ultimate open-ended performance invitation. You're already shuffling.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: ink+watercolor. Subject: yellow rabbit punching alarm clock in wrestling ring. Mood: designed chaos.

cards.power: Name it. Claim it. Power it. Show us what this Power does to reality right now.
cards.lore: The Intro isn't a character sheet. It's a promise. Say it like you mean it—the story starts the moment you commit.
cards.gradeReason: Four imperatives ending in "right now" — player IS performing before they finish reading.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: ink+watercolor. Subject: raccoons in luchador masks summoning character around ceremonial fire. Mood: performative commitment.

cards.power: Perform it. Don't calculate it. Play the contradiction.
cards.lore: Kayfabe means the fiction is real. Bizarro means the permission to be strange, wrong, and surprising on purpose.
cards.gradeReason: Entire deck philosophy in nine words. Immediate embodiment — no setup required.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: ink+watercolor. Subject: punk iguana burning rulebook on stage, one finger raised. Mood: principled permission.

cards.power: Play this to force the current storyteller to describe a completely mundane, ordinary routine for exactly one minute.
cards.lore: [Lore text degraded in PDF — OCR artifact on source file. Corrected: duration-based mundanity constraint.]
cards.gradeReason: "Exactly one minute" makes the boredom a timed performance act. Duration = embodiment.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: ink+watercolor. Subject: sloth in armchair reading newspaper, absolute stasis. Mood: mandatory mundanity.

cards.power: Play this to drastically change the relationship between two characters. Introduce a massive, unignorable problem.
cards.lore: A story goes nowhere until the hero gets in trouble. Break the routine. Present a mystery that must be solved.
cards.gradeReason: "Massive, unignorable problem" — you're already thinking of one before you put the card down.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: ink+watercolor. Subject: rhinoceros crashing through wall at sloth in armchair, both surprised. Mood: structural disruption.

cards.power: The active player must point to an object in the room and call it the first bizarre thing that comes to mind, incorporating it into the story instantly.
cards.lore: Open your mouth and allow anything to come out. Spontaneity is breaking the social conditioning that keeps you nice, safe, and boring.
cards.gradeReason: Physical pointing + instant incorporation — only card requiring player to engage the actual room.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: ink+watercolor. Subject: hedgehog surrounded by dynamite pointing at random object, explosion imminent. Mood: involuntary revelation.

cards.power: Play this to bring back an object, phrase, or character from the very first turn to instantly resolve the current conflict.
cards.lore: Make the audience feel like you planned this from the very beginning. You didn't. But you gave yourself the details to steal later.
cards.gradeReason: Technique is elegant; requires memory of earlier turns — procedural before it's performative.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: ink+watercolor. Subject: black raven returning with bloodied sword to confused scene. Mood: planted and retrieved.

cards.power: Play this to completely reject another player's narrative offer. The story stops dead.
cards.lore: Defense mechanisms that keep you safe in the real world make you absolutely terrible at games. Blocking kills the journey.
cards.gradeReason: Player IS the blocker — performing the improv failure mode while the card names exactly what they're doing.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: ink+watercolor. Subject: badger behind NO signs in military helmet, arms crossed. Mood: institutional refusal.

cards.power: Refuse to define what is happening in the scene. Stall the narrative indefinitely out of fear of being judged.
cards.lore: If you don't make a choice, nobody can tell you you're wrong. Why define the object when you can just play dead?
cards.gradeReason: "Play dead" — specific physical performance instruction embedded in the lore.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: ink+watercolor. Subject: possum under single spotlight, sweating, refusing to move. Mood: paralysis by judgment.

cards.power: Set up a brilliant narrative premise, then instantly wrap it in a bow and throw it in the trash before anyone else can interact with it.
cards.lore: I'm going to light a fire! Oh wait, the rain came and put it out. Crisis averted, story ruined.
cards.gradeReason: "Wrap it in a bow and throw it in the trash" is a physical metaphor delivered as direct performance act.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: ink+watercolor. Subject: tabby cat knocking water glass onto brilliant narrative premise mid-setup. Mood: preemptive self-sabotage.

cards.power: Force the narrative to reject a gift or idea, but demand the active player continues the story anyway.
cards.lore: No, I won't go to Grandma's. It's raining, the woods are dark, and she smells funny. Negative answers kill your partner's ideas.
cards.gradeReason: Lore is a ready-to-play script. The name lands before you finish the card.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: ink+watercolor. Subject: vulture under rain cloud at birthday cake, thumbs down. Mood: principled refusal of joy.

cards.power: Play this to force the current storyteller to describe three utterly irrelevant objects before they are allowed to finish their scene.
cards.lore: You aren't building a bridge, you're building a cage. Unnecessary steps ensure nobody ever has to be emotionally changed.
cards.gradeReason: Three irrelevant objects as prerequisite — specific number + specific irrelevance = bureaucratic trap enacted.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: ink+watercolor. Subject: beaver buried in red tape and requisition forms, can't see the bridge. Mood: process as prevention.

cards.power: Push a vital, high-stakes decision to the next player's turn so you don't have to take the creative risk yourself.
cards.lore: What are you going to say to him? I don't know, I'll think about it. Postponing a good idea to protect your ego.
cards.gradeReason: Name-to-mechanic match is instant. Every table has this player — card names them without making it personal.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: ink+watercolor. Subject: hedgehog curling at crossroads while high-stakes moment passes. Mood: strategic postponement.

cards.power: Hijack the Quest for a meaningless coffee break. Derail the main objective to discuss the weather.
cards.lore: Why hunt the Great Moose when we can stop at a diner and gossip for twenty minutes? The audience feels cheated.
cards.gradeReason: Squirrel metaphor does the work before you finish the title. Cheerful sabotage.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: ink+watercolor. Subject: squirrel abandoning Excalibur mid-extraction to chase shiny acorn. Mood: distracted heroism.

cards.power: Repeat the exact same action from the previous turn without advancing the plot or changing the emotional stakes.
cards.lore: Picking violets, then roses, then daffodils, then berries... a brilliant strategy to avoid anything actually happening.
cards.gradeReason: "Exact same action" — player is the loop, the instruction IS the critique of circular play.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: ink+watercolor. Subject: lemur on exercise wheel with internal monologue scrolling on rim. Mood: busy stasis.

cards.power: Derail the established genre entirely with a desperate, unearned attempt to look incredibly clever and avant-garde.
cards.lore: Please don't be clever. Be as boring as you possibly can. Trying to be original just derails the world we built together.
cards.gradeReason: Scare quotes around Original do all the work. "Desperate, unearned" — devastating precision.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: ink+watercolor. Subject: ostrich burying head in spaghetti noodles while wearing VR glasses in forest. Mood: performative confusion.

cards.power: Tell a terrible pun or one-liner to instantly escape a high-stakes, emotionally vulnerable scene.
cards.lore: Oh, what a grave situation! A joke is just a protective mechanism so the improviser doesn't have to experience real change.
cards.gradeReason: Player tells the bad pun — the escape from vulnerability IS the enacted failure mode. You know someone at your table.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: ink+watercolor. Subject: hyena on burning drum kit delivering rimshot pun to emotional scene. Mood: comedic cowardice.

cards.power: Spend your entire turn talking exclusively about a character or event that is not currently present on the Stage.
cards.lore: Talking about things that have already happened so you don't have to face the conflict standing right in front of you.
cards.gradeReason: Total Stage avoidance for an entire turn — duration + specificity make the deflection a performance.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: ink+watercolor. Subject: goose speaking into tin-can phone about absent parties, conflict visibly present and ignored. Mood: adjacent avoidance.

cards.power: Agree with the active player so hard, and with such identical emotional response, that further conflict becomes impossible.
cards.lore: I paint in exactly the same style! We should collaborate! Congratulations, you're playing nicely and the story is dead.
cards.gradeReason: "Story is dead" — lore delivers the punchline. Player kills the scene by agreeing perfectly.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: ink+watercolor. Subject: koala melded onto bear, dripping same paint colors, no friction possible. Mood: story death by harmony.

cards.power: You may not move your head while speaking this turn. Force the player next to you to break eye contact first.
cards.lore: Status has nothing to do with occupation. It is a fluid game of power. I am still, therefore I am in charge.
cards.gradeReason: Physical immobility + forced eye-contact break — most specific single-body performance instruction in the corpus.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: ink+watercolor. Subject: bulldog in suit perfectly still, color-splash behind, other player visibly folding. Mood: stillness as dominance.

cards.power: Fidget, giggle, and touch your face constantly. You automatically lose the current argument, but win the audience's sympathy.
cards.lore: Toes pointing in. Shoulders hunched. Hands drifting to the face. The epitome of the low-status climb.
cards.gradeReason: Lore is a body-language script. Three specific physical instructions — performing before you look up.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: ink+watercolor. Subject: nervous shrew in glasses fidgeting under spotlight, audience hearts visibly growing. Mood: sympathy through defeat.

cards.power: Instantly reverse the power dynamic of the current Stage. The lowest character becomes the highest, and vice versa.
cards.lore: We expect the high-status cop to pull over the low-status driver. Reversing it is where the comedy lives.
cards.gradeReason: Reversal IS the instruction — player enacts the structural inversion that generates the comedy.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: ink+watercolor. Subject: pig in overalls pointing at lion in sports car with parking ticket. Mood: structural comedy.

cards.power: Start your scene as the absolute, undisputed boss. End your scene humiliated in the metaphorical mud.
cards.lore: Tragedy is the high character falling. Comedy is the low character climbing. All drama is just a status seesaw.
cards.gradeReason: Full status arc in one instruction. You know start and end before you act.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: ink+watercolor. Subject: peacock in full display slowly sinking into mud as scene progresses. Mood: inevitable humiliation.

cards.power: Advance the narrative arc from Akt I (Setup) to the Ordeal, and finally to the Finale.
cards.lore: A story compass, not a countdown. As it rises, the dramatic weight shifts. You decide when to push hard or let it breathe.
cards.gradeReason: Narrative arc tracker — structurally essential but player action is Die advancement, not embodied character.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: ink+watercolor. Subject: exploding d20 with omega symbol, numbers and dramatic weight radiating. Mood: dramatic acceleration.

cards.power: Roll to force a strict narrative genre constraint on the current turn. You must commit to the tone.
cards.lore: The Mode is a frame, not a cage. If it creates a contradiction with your story—that is the story. Play the contradiction.
cards.gradeReason: "You must commit to the tone" demands performance; the dice roll makes commitment random rather than chosen.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: ink+watercolor. Subject: multicolour dice cube melting with comedy/tragedy masks on faces. Mood: genre as weather.

cards.power: Accept the most absurd, logic-breaking narrative offer given to you without a single moment of hesitation.
cards.lore: The number one reason we practice is trust. I know that when I step on stage, they have my back, and I have theirs.
cards.gradeReason: "Without a single moment of hesitation" — the hesitation IS the failure. Metaphor is the entire mechanic.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: ink+watercolor. Subject: two bears falling backward into each other blindfolded, thumbs up. Mood: practiced trust.

cards.power: Call KayfaBINGO! on another player's move to validate a perfect, spontaneous narrative beat.
cards.lore: We can make ourselves laugh all day long, but ultimately, the chaos demands a witness. We need someone to watch the work.
cards.gradeReason: Validation role is warm and important; player witnesses rather than generates — reactive rather than performative.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: ink+watercolor. Subject: crowd of meerkats leaning forward in wide-eyed delight. Mood: witnessed chaos.

cards.power: The story must suffer a genuine, irreversible loss this turn. No jokes. No escapes.
cards.lore: Loss is real. Push forward anyway. Let the tragedy breathe.
cards.gradeReason: "No jokes. No escapes." — the prohibition IS the performance demand. Hold the loss.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: ink+watercolor. Subject: elephant holding red sad balloon in rain, genuinely crying. Mood: held grief.

cards.power: Something goes terribly wrong in the scene, and it is explicitly, undeniably your character's fault.
cards.lore: Things go wrong. It's your fault. Play the gap between intention and catastrophic execution.
cards.gradeReason: "Explicitly, undeniably your fault" — no wiggle room, total ownership demanded immediately.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: ink+watercolor. Subject: dodo bird slipping on banana peel in disaster of its own making. Mood: earned catastrophe.

cards.power: Introduce a completely impossible, physics-breaking element to the scene and refuse to explain it or act surprised.
cards.lore: The impossible is normal. Don't explain it. Coherence is optional; connection matters more.
cards.gradeReason: "Refuse to explain it or act surprised" — the refusal is the specific performance. Fish in a suit: just Tuesday.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: ink+watercolor. Subject: salmon in tweed on penny-farthing drinking tea, completely blasé. Mood: normalised impossibility.

cards.power: Succeed against impossible, ridiculous odds with complete, unironic sincerity.
cards.lore: Your Character is right for this moment. Play the peak. Commit to the triumph, no matter how stupid the stakes.
cards.gradeReason: "Complete, unironic sincerity" — highest-difficulty emotional instruction in the Mode series. No winking allowed.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: ink+watercolor. Subject: corgi in cape standing on clifftop in lightning storm, absolute conviction. Mood: committed triumph.

cards.power: Reveal a hidden, cosmic, or supernatural layer operating directly beneath a mundane, boring interaction.
cards.lore: Something profound is happening beneath the surface. The diner coffee is actually the nectar of the underworld.
cards.gradeReason: Lore example IS the performance — diner coffee as underworld nectar shows the exact depth to find.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: ink+watercolor. Subject: galaxy-eyed owl seeing cosmic significance in a coffee cup. Mood: profound mundanity.

cards.power: Cross the exact social or narrative boundary the current scene has been politely tiptoeing around.
cards.lore: Make the table uncomfortable in a way that serves the story. Cross the line. Sell it.
cards.gradeReason: "Sell it." — two words that make this G1. Everyone knows where the forbidden line is. Zero ambiguity.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: ink+watercolor. Subject: skunk in front of DO NOT CROSS tape, crossing it with deliberate calm. Mood: deliberate transgression.

cards.power: Voluntarily kill off or eject your current character from the story to immediately draw and play a new one.
cards.lore: Voluntary drama. A good death scene is a gift to the story. Exit gracefully so someone else can enter.
cards.gradeReason: Death scene as gift is a beautiful invitation; needs character-draw system to be fully actionable.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: ink+watercolor. Subject: chameleon in tuxedo removing own head at microphone, new character waiting. Mood: gift of exit.

cards.power: Upon Quest Collapse, wipe all Scene cards from the Stage. Send everything to the discard pile. Start Akt 1 fresh.
cards.lore: The Finale doesn't have to be neat. It has to be true to what everyone built. A messy ending earned beats a neat ending imported. Then wipe it.
cards.gradeReason: Procedurally correct reset; Quest Collapse condition requires companion docs to trigger.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: ink+watercolor. Subject: large pink eraser wiping out entire comic storyboard, clean green space emerging. Mood: earned erasure.

cards.power: Yell this out of turn to validate another player's perfect, spontaneous narrative beat.
cards.lore: That landed. Spontaneous, no explanation needed. Laughter breaks nothing—if you're laughing, you're playing it right.
cards.gradeReason: "Yell this out of turn" — the out-of-turn physical act IS the card. Zero ambiguity.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: ink+watercolor. Subject: chihuahua slamming giant green button with both paws, sparks flying. Mood: involuntary validation.

cards.power: Yell this when a player uses game mechanics instead of storytelling. Force them to restate it as a narrative event.
cards.lore: Don't say 'I deal 3 damage.' Say 'Your empire glitches and seven kinds of collapse happen at once.' Perform, don't calculate.
cards.gradeReason: Lore gives exact before/after example. Accountability tool with no learning curve.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: ink+watercolor. Subject: gorilla on bongo drums roaring at metagamer. Mood: narrative enforcement.

cards.power: Pause the game to ask exactly one concrete question about a narrative gap. The active player must answer in 1–2 sentences.
cards.lore: Not a criticism. A question. Keep it short, keep it about the story, keep it kind. If someone is uncomfortable, boggle it.
cards.gradeReason: "Exactly one" + "1–2 sentences" + "keep it kind" — most precisely specified social act in the deck.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: ink+watercolor. Subject: pug with exposed brain, one question mark, genuinely confused. Mood: constructive bewilderment.

cards.power: Call out a broken rule, ignored mode, or out-of-character action. If the table agrees, the Quest Die freezes this turn.
cards.lore: A rule was broken. The fiction was breached. Nullify the progress. Call them out to protect the Kayfabe.
cards.gradeReason: Referee call with procedural consequence — necessary but reactive, needs Quest Die context.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: ink+watercolor. Subject: parrot in referee stripes holding yellow card. Mood: kayfabe protection.

cards.power: For this round, all direct narrative statements are forbidden. Every piece of dialogue and narration must be a question.
cards.lore: Wer eine Aussage macht, verliert den Zug. The Quest Die drops. Active listening forced through grammatical sabotage.
cards.gradeReason: Total grammatical mode change — classic improv game understood at any table, zero explanation needed.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: ink+watercolor. Subject: praying mantis under interrogation lamp, all dialogue bubbles ending in question marks. Mood: forced inquiry.

cards.power: Scream 'NEW CHOICE!' to force the active player to instantly rewrite and replace their last sentence with something entirely different.
cards.lore: The original was boring. Do it again, but weirder. Practice taking correction without losing face.
cards.gradeReason: Legendary improv game. "Scream" is the physical instruction — the card is the call is the mechanic.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: ink+watercolor. Subject: red octopus with megaphone surrounded by genre clapperboards. Mood: relentless redirection.

cards.power: Draw a random genre card. The current scene MUST instantly pivot to match the tropes of that genre.
cards.lore: Suddenly... a bureaucratic office thriller! Watch how framing violently alters the exact same story.
cards.gradeReason: "MUST instantly pivot" — no lag, no negotiation. Pivot IS the performance of genre embodiment.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: ink+watercolor. Subject: cowboy-astronaut chameleon half-Western half-sci-fi, clapperboard in hand. Mood: violent genre accommodation.

cards.power: Force a player to seamlessly weave a random, pre-written, completely absurd sentence into their monologue.
cards.lore: The ambassador has already shipped the bananas. Now make it make sense in our medieval fantasy scene. Irgendwie.
cards.gradeReason: Banana example demonstrates the challenge. "Seamlessly weave" + "completely absurd" is named and shown.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: ink+watercolor. Subject: mole in glasses receiving absurd secret message, reading it with complete commitment. Mood: mandatory integration.

cards.power: Force the table to play the exact same scene three times: Normal, Flawless Success, and Absolute Catastrophe.
cards.lore: Drei Leben einer Story. Play the Deus Ex Machina, then play the total collapse. At the end, ask: which version was ehrlicher?
cards.gradeReason: Three-part structure crystal clear. "Ehrlicher" (more honest) IS the learning outcome — bilingual punchline.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: ink+watercolor. Subject: two-faced coin (angel/devil) with gold and dark halves balanced. Mood: three-version honesty.

cards.power: Yell FREEZE! Assume the exact physical posture of the active player, and use that pose to start a completely different scene.
cards.lore: Physical pantomime as the ultimate narrative hijack. The old scene is paused; the new reality overwrites it.
cards.gradeReason: Most kinetically specific card in the corpus. Assume exact physical posture of another player — body IS the new story.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: ink+watercolor. Subject: penguin frozen mid-gesture in ice cube, another penguin outside beginning entirely different pantomime. Mood: body as portal.

cards.power: Narrate a scene using ONLY silent physical gestures. The next player must interpret the pantomime aloud to continue the story.
cards.lore: Stille Post mit Konsequenzen. The difference between your narrative intent and their spoken impact is the punchline.
cards.gradeReason: "ONLY silent physical gestures" — absolute prohibition makes this one of the purest embodiment cards in the deck.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: ink+watercolor. Subject: five monkeys in telephone-game chain, panic growing with each misinterpretation. Mood: translation entropy.

cards.power: Overwrite a full Stage slot. Re-frame what was there completely. Yes-and, not yes-but-actually-no.
cards.lore: Nothing gets erased, just reframed. Sometimes the bulldozer is the only valid literary device.
cards.gradeReason: Philosophically loaded ("yes-and") but player action is Stage slot administration — system-dependent.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: ink+watercolor. Subject: yellow bulldozer pushing colorful Stage cards off cliff into reframed reality. Mood: valid demolition.

cards.power: Force the active player to introduce a narrative contradiction. The Quest Die cannot rise until the contradiction is resolved.
cards.lore: Not 'Yes, and'—but 'Yes, but actually...' Dialectical thinking where conflict is the only engine.
cards.gradeReason: Forced contradiction with mechanical stake (Die frozen) — player generates and holds the tension.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: ink+watercolor. Subject: badger barrister in wig slamming gavel on contract. Mood: productive contradiction.

cards.power: Divide the physical table into four zones (Realism, Absurdism, Mythos, Satire). Where you place your card dictates the genre.
cards.lore: Place it on the border. I dare you to mix Realism and Satire. Context interprets action. Consistency will be socially negotiated.
cards.gradeReason: "Divide the physical table" — player transforms the actual game surface into a performance space.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: ink+watercolor. Subject: tortoise shell divided into four vivid genre zones. Mood: spatial negotiation.

cards.power: Restrict a player's entire vocabulary for the session to 10 specific word tokens. They must pay to borrow words from others.
cards.lore: Deine Worte, nicht meine. To speak freely, you must pay the Quest Die a tax. Wessen Sprache bestimmt die Realität?
cards.gradeReason: Brilliant concept; 10 word token setup and economic structure hold it at G2 — needs table prep.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: ink+watercolor. Subject: magpie rearranging letter tiles on corkboard: GIVE ME TIME. Mood: language as property.

cards.power: Seize absolute, dictatorial control over all rules disputes at the table for exactly one turn.
cards.lore: Final call on any argument. A crown made of fast-food paper. Most tables won't need this. Yours probably will.
cards.gradeReason: "Yours probably will." — lore closes the deal. Crown yourself immediately with whatever is available.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: ink+watercolor. Subject: frog in paper fast-food crown, absolute sovereign certainty. Mood: necessary dictatorship.

cards.power: Begin a grand, mythic quest that immediately gets sidetracked by a mundane complaint about a coffee shop.
cards.lore: We are hunting a myth, but first, let's complain about the weather for twenty minutes. A masterpiece of Sidetracking.
cards.gradeReason: Complete scene setup in one sentence. You're already complaining about the weather.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: editorial ink. Subject: moose at diner counter next to hero who is complaining about the coffee. Mood: adjacent heroism.

cards.power: Force two characters into an incredibly awkward first date scenario filled with twitching and terrible questions.
cards.lore: Can I have your meatballs? Do you drink alcohol? Every day. A one-minute masterclass in terrible status play.
cards.gradeReason: "Twitching and terrible questions" — both physical and verbal instructions for status catastrophe.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: editorial ink. Subject: rat waiter in tuxedo presenting meatballs to awkward couple at candlelit table. Mood: status disaster theatre.

cards.power: Escalate a minor medical or personal issue into a full-blown sci-fi horror event in a single sentence.
cards.lore: Positive forward movement does not mean happy. Raise the stakes so high the audience can't look away.
cards.gradeReason: "In a single sentence" — time constraint makes this a high-difficulty, zero-ambiguity performance challenge.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: editorial ink. Subject: pelican doctor holding X-ray showing alien embryo, both equally shocked. Mood: medical escalation.

cards.power: End a scene with the most unearned, absurd, gravity-defying Deus Ex Machina possible.
cards.lore: Because getting hit by a ton of wet pasta is technically a conclusion. A monument to the desperate desire to be original.
cards.gradeReason: "Technically a conclusion" — name IS the example. Player knows exactly how absurd to be.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: editorial ink. Subject: wet spaghetti meteor impact on forest picnic, red sauce explosion. Mood: unearned resolution.

cards.power: [ Write your own cynical sabotage here ]
cards.lore: [ Accuse your friends of something specific here ]
cards.gradeReason: "Accuse your friends of something specific" — best blank-card framing in the deck; execution requires player content.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: ink+watercolor. Subject: watercolour explosion on blank canvas, no subject. Mood: potential.

cards.power: [ Break the game intentionally here ]
cards.lore: [ Blame Uncle FrizzleBob for the consequences here ]
cards.gradeReason: "Blame Uncle FrizzleBob for the consequences" — beautiful meta-instruction even when blank.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: ink+watercolor. Subject: animals with blank signs marching. Mood: intentional vacuum.

cards.power: [ Define a new emotional cage for your table ]
cards.lore: [ Roll D6 to suffer the consequences ]
cards.gradeReason: "Emotional cage" + "Roll D6 to suffer the consequences" — most functional blank card; playable even empty.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: editorial ink. Subject: glowing white cube in pen-and-ink void. Mood: undefined potential.

cards.power: Scan the eyeball to download the apocalypse (Extensions, Lore, Add-ons). Kayfabizarro trusts you. If it's broken, fix it. If it's missing, add it. Destroy this book. Stay fluffy.
cards.lore: Kayfabizarro trusts you. If it's broken, fix it. If it's missing, add it. Destroy this book. Stay fluffy.
cards.gradeReason: "Destroy this book. Stay fluffy." — most liberating game-ending instruction in the corpus.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: editorial ink. Subject: old man with QR-code eyeball giving thumbs up, warm light radiating. Mood: final permission.

verdict: The Improv Comedy SKETCHBOOK is the performance engine at the heart of the Kayfabizarro system — where the political decks tell you what to think, this one tells you how to embody it. G1=73% is earned and structural: every villain card (cards 09–20) forces the player to inhabit the failure mode they're supposed to avoid, which is pedagogical Übererfüllung at its finest. Named strength: SPACE JUMP (Freeze!) and The High-Status Hound are internationally legible improv instructions that need zero system context. Named weakness: the three blank template cards on page 15 are placeholder energy in a deck that otherwise doesn't mess around — fill or remove before a major push. Table-ready: YES. Hand this to a first-timer.
blurb: For improv groups, drama teachers, and anyone who has ever wanted to name exactly what is killing the scene. Cards that coach and cards that play — 60 unhinged instructions in one sketchbook.

coverQA.coverVisual: 4 — FrizzleBob rabbit painting CORPORATE REALITY on sketchbook page, yellow background pops against the ink-splatter aesthetic
coverQA.coverTitle: 4 — SKETCHBOOK framing is honest and on-brand; sets clear expectations without overselling
coverQA.coverVibeMatch: 5 — chaotic painterly energy matches the improv-chaos theme precisely; cover IS the deck
coverQA.coverOriginality: 4 — distinctly FrizzleBob, unmistakable in the Kayfabizarro universe
coverQA.coverViral: 3 — SKETCHBOOK positions it as a working tool, undersells the party/performance potential
coverQA.coverNote: Rabbit's got the right energy and the title delivers exactly what it promises. SKETCHBOOK frames it as a working tool rather than a party product — accurate but underselling the performance chaos inside. The yellow background says comedy before the text loads.

notes: 15 pages, 4 cards per page (2×2 grid), 60 cards total. No dedicated cover page — p.1 contains first 4 cards including title card. No back cover. Sidebar decorative callouts (KayfaBINGO!, BLÖDSINN!, HUMBUG!, What the FLUFF?!, Stay fluffy!, KayfaBOGGLE!, KayfaBIZARRO!) appear in page margins as layout elements — not card content. FONT ARTIFACTS (2): Card 05 (The Boring Stasis) lore text degraded in PDF due to AI-rendered font OCR failure; card 60 (The Final Blessing) power text has 'truets' = 'trusts'. marketingText:
Kayfabizarro: THE IMPROV KOMEDY SKETCHBOOK – Name What's Killing the Scene, Then Throw It (Free Cut & Play Comic Card Game)

Two players, one suggestion, and a four-second hole where a scene used to be. Everybody at the table felt it die. Nobody in the room has ever had the exact word for what did it.

That is the part no workshop fixes. Improv gets taught like table manners: say yes, support your partner, never block. All true, all useless the second the scene goes limp and polite and nobody can say why. You walk out with a vague feeling and a note you cannot act on, a funnier version of yourself still stuck behind the fear of being the one who names it out loud.

This Sketchbook splits the deck in two. Half the cards play you, throwing a move onto the stage you have to commit to on the spot. The other half coach you, putting a name on the exact thing strangling the scene so the table can call it and fix it mid-bit. That is Social Story Wrestling pointed straight at the improv stage: sixty cut-and-play cards, a status game running underneath every one of them, and a room that decides whether you raised the scene or sandbagged it.

WHAT'S INSIDE?
- The Sketchbook Core Deck: 60 High-Res "Print, Cut & Play" Cards, featuring SPACE JUMP (Freeze!), The High-Status Hound, and The Golden Rule of Bizarro.
- The Freestyle Rules: the complete Anti-Rulebook. No complicated math, just storytelling, RAF dice that rule how hard the bit lands, and the coach-or-play split that lets the table referee a scene while it is still breathing.
- The Status Engine: the spine of the whole deck, where high-status and low-status stop being theory and turn into moves you can point at, hand off, or get caught dodging. The margin calls, KayfaBINGO!, BLÖDSINN!, HUMBUG!, What the FLUFF?!, are how the room heckles in real time.

THE "LIVING DECK" PASS (Free Updates)
Grab this once and you are not buying a frozen PDF. You are on the manifest for the Kayfabizarro main line. Every future expansion, every new coaching card and status move added to the cycle, lands in your library as a free update, no second checkout.

WHY "PAY WHAT YOU WANT"?
I draw these for the rooms that go polite instead of funny, and for the drama teacher wrangling thirty kids with no shared word for what just flopped. This deck hands you both halves: the nerve to throw the first move, and the language to name what sank the last one. Broke? Enter "0" and take it. Print it, cut it, run it at the next rehearsal until the dead air stops getting the last word. Want to support the craft? Every dollar goes straight into the time I spend drawing the next cards and sharpening the next rules. Free to use, share, and adapt under CC BY-NC-SA 4.0. Share freely, attribute honestly, never resell.

Choose your reality. Become an Epistemic Outlaw.
"Nobody kills a scene on purpose. That is the whole reason you need a card that can name it."
Stay fluffy. — Uncle FrizzleBob
